subject: Discovery recap — service principals, short-lived tokens, and SDK onboarding
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Malik <sara.malik@finedge.com>, James Park <james.park@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — service principals, short-lived tokens, and SDK onboarding

Hi Sara / James —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the recommended integration path so you have a single place to share with your infra/security team. I tried to keep this focused on the decisions we talked through and the immediate next steps for a small POC.

What we heard / constraints
- Need least-privilege credentials for app servers that will call Redwood APIs (not end-user tokens).
- Rotation and auditability are top requirements for your security/compliance team.
- You plan to use embeddings + a lightweight reranker in the pipeline; latency budget ~150ms p50 for reranking step.
- Potential preference for using your KMS/HSM for signing keys.

Recommended integration pattern (consolidated)
1) Service principal model (recommended): create a FinEdge service account in your IdP, use short-lived JWTs obtained via client_credentials -> STS exchange. Tokens include aud = "redwood-inference" and a kid header referencing a signing key stored in your KMS.
   - TTL: we recommend 1h tokens for prod, 15m tokens for high-security workloads.
   - Rotation: rotate signing keys in KMS on a weekly cadence and revoke via key versioning; Redwood accepts OIDC/JWTs and can verify using your JWKS endpoint.
2) Fallback API key for early POC only: create a scoped API key with minimal permissions and strict IP and time constraints; rotate daily and treat as ephemeral.
3) Private deployment note: if you go with Redwood Private (VPC), we can support HSM-backed signing for client-side verification and establish mutual TLS for admin endpoints.

Auth-specific implementation notes
- Use token exchange (client_credentials + STS) so you never store long-lived secrets on the app server.
- Include a claims field listing scopes (e.g., embeddings:read, model:invoke) to enforce least privilege.
- For service accounts, provide a role mapping doc so we can map FinEdge roles to Redwood API permissions.

Integration pieces Redwood will provide
- SDK quickstart (Node + Python) with helper to fetch short-lived tokens from your STS and attach Authorization: Bearer <jwt>.
- Example routing config for embeddings -> reranker flow (use rwd-rerank-lite as initial model).
- Template for a minimal audit log forwarder if you want consolidated event delivery to your SIEM.

Proposed next steps / owners
- FinEdge: confirm which IdP you’ll use and whether you expose a JWKS/STS endpoint (action: Sara).
- Redwood: produce SDK quickstart and a one-page security note describing verification and rotation (action: Marissa & Ben).
- Align on POC timeline: week of Aug 8 suggested.

Attachments: I’m sending the SDK quickstart + a short MVP checklist in the follow-up.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a quick follow-up with your security lead.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — this is super helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we circulate to infra/security: 

1) When you say 'token exchange / STS', do you mean Redwood will accept tokens signed by our KMS (we'll expose a JWKS) and validate them directly? Or do you expect us to mint tokens via an intermediate exchange service?

2) For the 'role mapping doc' — can you provide the exact permission granularity you need? We do least-privilege via roles in our IdP and would like to map 1:1 where possible.

3) HSM question — we prefer signing keys in an HSM. Does Redwood need to store any private key material? If not, that's a win for us.

4) POC timeline: week of Aug 8 is fine. Can you confirm the estimated time for Redwood's SDK quickstart delivery?

If you want to pull in our security engineer (Nathan) I can loop him into the next thread.

— Sara
Sara Malik

My thoughts / suggested owners: 
- Q1: Redwood can validate tokens directly from your JWKS. We also support token-exchange flows if you prefer a short-lived service token model; either works. (Owner: Marissa) — ETA: 48 hours for a short explainer.
- Q2: I'll draft a permission matrix for common API actions (embeddings.create, model.invoke, logs.read) so we can map to FinEdge roles. (Owner: Ben) — ETA: 3 business days.
- Q3: Redwood does not need to store your private key. We verify signatures against your JWKS (public keys). If you want mutual TLS or an HSM-backed provisioning handshake for Private deployments, that's a separate step. (Owner: Ben) — include as note in the security doc.
- Q4: SDK quickstart — let's aim to have a Node + Python snippet and a markdown quickstart by Monday (Aug 1). (Owner: Marissa)

Please add any constraints I missed. I'll respond to Sara with the ETA once we confirm.

Hi Sara / James —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (Node + Python snippets) and the MVP integration checklist. Highlights below and answers to your Qs.

Answers to your Qs
- JWKS / STS: Redwood can validate JWTs directly against your JWKS endpoint (no private key sharing). If you prefer an STS exchange, our quickstart includes an example where your app exchanges a short-lived credential for a Redwood-scoped token.
- Permission granularity: see the attached permission matrix (summary in checklist). Typical scopes we recommend: 
  - embeddings:read
  - embeddings:write (if you push vectors)
  - models:invoke
  - logs:read (audit only)
  - admin:deploy (if you want model rollouts)
We can accept either scope-based claims or an array of role strings; we'll map at onboarding.
- HSM / private keys: Redwood does NOT require your private key material. Provide a public JWKS and we verify signatures. For Private deployments, we can arrange an HSM-backed handshake — we’ll follow up if you go that route.

Recommended prod settings for rotation / TTL
- Token TTL: 1 hour (prod), 15 minutes (high-security).
- Rotation cadence for signing keys: weekly rotate with immediate revocation via key versioning.
- API key: Only for POC, restricted by IP and TTL = 24 hours, then rotate.

Embedding/reranker routing suggestion
- Route user queries to embeddings endpoint first, perform a nearest-neighbors filter, then call the rwd-rerank-lite model for the top-k candidates. We included a sample routing.conf in the quickstart. This flow keeps p50 latency within your 150ms target for small top-k sizes.

POC plan / timeline
- Aug 1: SDK quickstart + checklist (attached) — COMPLETE
- Aug 3–6: FinEdge infra validation and JWKS/STSc endpoint availability (your action)
- Week of Aug 8: Redwood partner POC — we’ll do a 2-hour kickoff and run a small integration against a sandbox dataset.

Action items (explicit)
- FinEdge: share JWKS URL and confirm which IdP role maps to 'service:ingest' (owner: Sara) — due Aug 4.
- FinEdge: confirm whether you want HSM-backed signing or standard JWKS (owner: James) — due Aug 4.
- Redwood: provide security note + permission matrix (owner: Ben) — due Aug 3.
- Redwood: deliver Node + Python quickstart (owner: Marissa) — delivered (attachment).

Attachments included as stubs: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md, mvp-integration-checklist.xlsx. Also attaching a draft SOW for signature if you want to accelerate (DocuSign link below).
